Since then the generator's 13 October 2026 transformations (constant_range in editorial/generate_companion.py) have generalized assertions of Chapters 1 and 13 from the fixed pair c₁ = 10^-4, c₂ = 1/2 to every 0 < c₁ ≤ 1/3, c₁ < c₂ < 1 (proved: LUniform.uniform_global_failure, LUniform.uniformSmoothLocalFailure); not a change made by the opening, but see the note on line 62.

items.anchor: The revised article independently proves global centered and coercive homogeneous convergence, local finite-partition and planar results, the actual-matrix framework and both finite-branch local counterexamples.
items.note: The results proved in the article (paper/): centered and coercive homogeneous global convergence, the local finite polyhedral partition theorem and its PLQ corollary, the planar cluster/convergence/smooth-max results and the nonradial example, the actual-matrix framework (principal-minor hierarchy, reciprocal growth, transported certificate) and the two finite-branch local counterexamples (four C^{2,1} branches; four uniformly strongly convex C^{1,1} branches). "Independently": the article's proofs do not rely on the companion (editorial).

items.anchor: The noncompact homogeneous alternatives, fixed-normal geometry, flat-contour parabolic family, lifting, rates and scalar baseline remain separate companion results.
items.note: Noncompact homogeneous alternatives: Theorems 7.A and 7.C; fixed-normal geometry: Theorems 11.1 and 11.2; flat-contour parabolic family: the theorem of Chapter 10; lifting: F:lifting and (7.7.1); rates: the little-o rates of Section 6.5 (along runs with bounded gradients, W1/W24; the summary only names them); scalar baseline: the scalar convergence proposition of Chapter 5 (P8 of the introduction). "Separate companion results": the article does not state them (editorial).

items.anchor: The infinite constant-Hessian family in Chapter~\ref{comp:L} also remains here
items.note: The sentence "The infinite constant-Hessian family in Chapter 13 also remains here after its removal from the article's main theorem selection." The family is Theorem L:thm:global (for every μ > 0, Q_μ with constant branch Hessians μI). History: the article no longer lists it among its main theorems, but keeps the same family (Q_μ for every μ > 0 with its bad orbits near the wrong corner) as the supporting Proposition art:quadratic_failure of its appendix (A/lower_curvature/proposition/art:quadratic_failure); "removal from the article's main theorem selection" is accurate in that sense.

items.anchor: None of these incomparable results is treated as superseded merely because the article selects a smaller statement set.
items.reason: Editorial policy (supersession).
items.note: The policy (no listed result is treated as superseded) is editorial. Wording point (hand-written file; review F7): "incomparable" is inaccurate for two of the listed results. The constant-Hessian family of Chapter 13 (L:thm:global) is the family of the article's appendix Proposition art:quadratic_failure (the same Q_μ for every μ > 0, the same bad orbit; the sentence of lines 20-22 says only that it left the main theorem selection), so the article's selection contains it. The consequences of Theorem 7.A for bounded-below and coercive objectives (C/07_H/prose/007-008) give the article's Theorem art:homogeneous, so that family contains an article result. Proposed: correspondence.tex:22, old string "None of these incomparable results" (1 occurrence; "incomparable" also occurs at line 32, in the table row on the supersession ledger, which is not concerned) -> "None of these results".
